A1.justification: Both complete, readable 11-page PDFs describe Sonic. Their scientific text, equations, figures, and tables support direct comparison. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, qualitative generation results, a 40-participant user study, and ablations in Section 4, Tables 1–4, and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, qualitative evaluations, 40-participant user study, and ablations reported in v1.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain identical context-enhanced audio learning, motion-decoupled control, and time-aware position shift fusion. No algorithm, architecture, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Training coverage remains VFHQ, CelebV-Text, and VoxCeleb2; benchmark evaluation remains HDTF and CelebV-HQ. The portrait styles, speech/singing/rap inputs, and extended-duration generation scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SadTalker, AniPortrait, V-Express, Hallo, Hallo2, and EchoMimic. Comparator membership in the user study and the motion-frame/overlap comparisons in Tables 2 and 4 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain 100 HDTF and 50 CelebV-HQ four-second test clips, identical evaluation metrics and model settings, and the same 40-participant study using scores from 1 to 5.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 and Figure 6 retain identical component ablations, dynamic-scale comparisons, shift-offset analysis, long-video inference comparisons, and controls over lip, expression, and head movement.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Both present point estimates without reported repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results, qualitative examples, and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Sonic's HDTF FID/FVD of 29.104/301.173 and CelebV-HQ FID/FVD of 43.137/483.108.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), the mathematical descriptions of attention and motion control, and the computational-cost analysis in Section 3.3 are identical. No definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about global audio perception, video quality, temporal consistency, lip synchronization, and motion diversity.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 retain the same mechanism explanations, interpretations of long-video consistency, and tradeoffs associated with extreme control parameters. No limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: The backbone, audio features, condition dropout, guidance settings, motion parameters, and inference details remain identical. The project-page access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged. All 52 reference entries match after whitespace normalization; their movement across pages does not add or remove cited works.

P1.justification: v2 adds a 22-name Contributors paragraph after the conclusion on page 9 and updates the printed arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: The contributor paragraph shifts the References heading downward and reflows reference entries across pages 9–11. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–4 retain identical content, formatting, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds contributor credit and updates the version stamp, with limited reference-page reflow. These attribution and presentation updates leave the scientific exposition, evidence, claims, and reproducibility information identical, producing no meaningful change in overall paper quality.
